acceptance: A dry run on an aborted batch lists the integration and member worktrees and branches it would remove.
EXECUTE=1 removes them with expected-OID branch deletion and refuses dirty, locked or unrecorded-commit cases, with tests.
docs/agent/batch-feature-delivery.md documents the aborted-batch cleanup step.
description:
Problem. After abort_batch, the integration and member worktrees remain and no repository tool removes them. make batch-finish refuses: 'the batch lifecycle is aborted, not completed; finish it first'. make worktree-finish holds the integration worktree: 'No merged PR found for branch feat/sqlglot-core-delivery (found 1 unmerged PRs)', because the aborted batch's final PR (#3975) was closed, and the member branches never had PRs. Observed for batch sqlglot-core-delivery (worktrees BenchBox.wt-sqlglot-core-delivery, --adoption, --consumer), whose content shipped through a re-registered batch in #3980. The only remaining route is a manual git worktree remove and branch delete, which agents may not run without owner approval.

Change. Give batch-finish (or a batch-cleanup target) an aborted-lifecycle mode that previews and, with EXECUTE=1, removes the integration and member worktrees and deletes their local branches with expected-OID checks, refusing dirty or locked worktrees and branches with unpushed commits not reachable from a recorded head.
